action: Do not administer ARNi concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi
action_detail: Concomitant use of ARNi with ACEi is contraindicated due to risk of angioedema from dual inhibition of neprilysin and ACE pathways, both of which degrade bradykinin. A 36-hour washout period is required when switching between ACEi and ARNi.
source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last ACEi dose
action_detail: Sacubitril/Valsartan (the only approved ARNi) must not be given with any ACEi. Omapatrilat (a combined neprilysin/ACE inhibitor) showed unacceptable angioedema rates in RCTs, leading to its development termination. The mechanism involves dual inhibition of bradykinin degradation by both ACE and neprilysin pathways.
source_text: Oral neprilysin inhibitors, used in combination with ACEi, can lead to angioedema, and concomitant use is contraindicated. An ARNi should not be administered within 36 hours of switching from or to an ACEi. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Do not administer Sacubitril/Valsartan with Enalapril
action_detail: In PARADIGM-HF, sacubitril/valsartan was compared with enalapril. Concomitant use of neprilysin inhibitors with ACEi leads to angioedema via dual bradykinin pathway inhibition. A 36-hour washout is required when switching between these agents.
source_text: Oral neprilysin inhibitors, used in combination with ACEi, can lead to angioedema, and concomitant use is contraindicated and should be avoided. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)
